newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ESTES PUTS EXCLAMATION POINT ON ALL-STAR STATUS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ESTES PUTS EXCLAMATION POINT ON ALL-STAR STATUS.

text.p: Shawn Estes put an exclamation mark on his All-Star status as he gave up one hit over 8 2/3 innings and struck out 11 Friday as the Giants handed the Colorado Rockies their fourth straight loss, 4-0.

Estes (12-2), walked two batters, both in the ninth, and came within one out of his third shutout of the season. The only hit he yielded was a one-out single in the first to Quinton McCracken, who was thrown out stealing.
The 24-year-old left-hander retired the next 22 hitters before a leadoff walk to Kirt Manwaring in the ninth.
"I had my best stuff tonight," said Estes, who has given up just four runs in his last 29 2/3 innings. "They're an agressive team and that helps me a lot, I throw to areas and they just swing."
Said Giants manager Dusty Baker in admiration: "It seems like he's getting better."
Colorado manager Don Baylor said Estes frustrated his hard-hitting club.

"It seems like he just paralysed our right-handed guys with breaking balls," said Baylor. "At Coors Field, he went after us with fastballs, tonight he changed patterns, if a pitcher does that, than the hitters have to make adjustments."
Jeff Kent hit his 18th homer of the season for the Giants.

In St Louis, Mark Smith hit a two-run homer off Dennis Eckersley in the top of the 10th after Tony Womack's gift double tied it with two out in the ninth as the Pittsburgh Pirates overcame the Cards 7-5 for their fifth win in a row.
In the ninth, Eckersley (0-3) was one out away from his 18th save before left fielder Ron Gant misplayed Womack's line drive into a double, scoring Jose Guillen from second.

"This had to be the most frustrating loss in my time with the Cardinals," St. Louis manager Tony La Russa said. "Here we had a game gift wrapped and the sun gets in our fielder's eyes. What can you say, it was just a frustrating game for everyone."
Marc Wilkins (6-1) threw a scoreless ninth to take the win for the Pirates, who moved into a tie with the Cardinals for first place in the Central Division.

In New York, Todd Pratt, making his first major-league appearance in nearly two years, and Bernard Gilkey both homered and drove in three runs as the Mets ended a four-game losing streak with a 6-2 win over the Florida Marlins.

Pratt, brought up from the minors Thursday when All-Star catcher Todd Hundley experienced soreness in his right elbow, hit a two-run homer in the second off starter Al Leiter (7-6) to lift New York into a 2-2 tie.
Gilkey, mired in a season-long slump, added a two-run homer in the fifth and an RBI single in the eighth.
Rick Reed (7-6) went six innings for the win.
In Montreal, Mark Lemke snapped a tie with a bloop two-run triple down the left-field line in the top of the ninth inning as the Atlanta Braves beat the Montreal Expos 6-3.
Brad Clontz (4-1) worked a scoreless inning for the win and Mark Wohlers notched his 19th save. Ugueth Urbina (2-6), in relief of Carlos Perez, took the loss.
The Braves have won all six meetings with the Expos this season and are 16-3 against them over the last two seasons.
Braves first baseman Fred McGriff left in the fourth inning with a strained right hamstring, and Montreal's Henry Rodriguez exited in the third with a lower back strain.

In San Diego, Pedro Astacio allowed two runs over 6 1/3 innings to defeat San Diego for the second time this week and Greg Gagne and Tripp Cromer each had two hits and two RBI, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 5-2 win over the Padres.
Scott Radinsky and Darren Dreifort combined for 1 2/3 scoreless innings and Todd Worrell allowed one hit with a strikeout in the ninth for his 19th save.

In Philadelphia, a meeting with his former club was just what Cubs' starter Terry Mulholland needed to notch his first victory in over a month as Chicago handed the hapless Philadelphia Phillies their 11th straight loss, 9-3.
Chicago extended its season-high winning streak to five games while handing the Phillies their 19th loss in 20 games.
"You could use all kinds of adjectives," said Phillies' manager Terry Francona.
"Frustrated, irritated, but above all, because I care a lot, the one word we can't use is quit. The day we quit is the day we got serious problems, and that won't happen."
Mulholland improved to 6-9.
In Houston, Willie Greene crushed a three-run homer and Mike Morgan won for the first time since May 26 as the Cincinnati Reds won their season-high fifth straight game, 4-2 over the Houston Astros.

Greene hit his 12th homer in the fourth inning off Houston starter Tommy Greene (0-1) as the Reds rallied from a 2-0 deficit. The ball reached the upper deck in right field at the Astrodome, only the third ball ever to do so in right field.
"Greene's homer was a monumental blast," Cincinnati manager Ray Knight said. "I played here for three years and was in the league for 12 and have not ever seen a ball hit that far in this park.
Morgan (3-5) allowed two runs over five innings.
